about: Majid Al Futtaim Properties is the real estate arm of Majid Al Futtaim Holding, the Dubai conglomerate. It develops and operates Mall of the Emirates, City Centre malls across the Middle East and Africa, and community developments including Tilal Al Ghaf and Aljada, plus hotels and leisure venues such as Ski Dubai. Revenue comes from rent, hospitality and property sales, serving retail tenants and millions of shoppers annually. The group also runs Carrefour franchise stores across the region. High consumer visibility, frequent event sponsor in the UAE.

wiki.title: Majid Al Futtaim Group
wiki.text: Majid Al Futtaim Holding is an Emirati holding company based in Dubai. The family-owned conglomerate owns and operates shopping malls, retail, and hotel establishments in the Middle East and North Africa.

about: Cushman & Wakefield is a global commercial real estate services firm, founded in 1917 and headquartered in Chicago, offering leasing, capital markets, property and facility management, valuation and consulting for office, industrial, retail and other property owners and occupiers. It has around 50,000 employees and roughly 400 offices in about 60 countries, with annual revenue near 10 billion dollars. It is listed on the NYSE as CWK. A B2B brand with moderate corporate recognition, and it has sponsored sport and business events.

wiki.title: Cushman & Wakefield
wiki.what: Global commercial real estate services firm
wiki.text: Cushman & Wakefield is a global commercial real estate services firm headquartered in Chicago, Illinois. The company provides services to occupiers and investors and, as of 2025, had approximately 53,000 employees across more than 350 offices in nearly 60 countries. In 2025, Cushman & Wakefield reported revenue of $10.3 billion, with operations across services, leasing, capital markets, and valuation and other advisory services.

about: World's largest flooring manufacturer, producing carpet, ceramic tile, laminate, vinyl, hardwood and stone under brands such as Mohawk, Karastan, Daltile, Unilin and Quick-Step. It sells to homeowners and contractors via retailers, home centres, designers and builders across the US, Europe, Latin America and elsewhere, with revenue near 11 billion dollars and roughly 40,000 employees. NYSE-listed (MHK) and based in Calhoun, Georgia. Familiar to consumers who buy flooring.

wiki.title: Mohawk Industries
wiki.text: Mohawk Industries is an American flooring manufacturer based in Calhoun, Georgia. Mohawk produces floor covering products for residential and commercial applications in North America and residential applications in Europe. The company manufacturing portfolio consists of soft flooring products, hard flooring products, laminate flooring, sheet vinyl and luxury vinyl tile, natural stone and quartz countertops. In Europe, the company also produces and sells insulation, panels and mezzanine flooring. The company employs 40,500 people in operations in Australia, Brazil, Canada, Europe, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Russia and the United States. A

about: Vingroup is Vietnam's largest private conglomerate, founded by billionaire Pham Nhat Vuong and headquartered in Hanoi. It spans real estate through Vinhomes and Vincom Retail, hospitality and resorts under Vinpearl, healthcare via Vinmec, education with Vinschool and VinUniversity, and electric vehicles through VinFast, which listed on Nasdaq in 2023 and sells cars in Vietnam, the US, Canada and Europe. Vingroup is listed on the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange (VIC) and employs tens of thousands. Very strong consumer brand across Vietnam and growing international visibility through VinFast, which has sponsored football events.

wiki.title: Vingroup
wiki.text: Vingroup JSC is a private Vietnamese conglomerate owned by entrepreneur Phạm Nhật Vượng as the largest shareholder, and headquartered in Long Bien district, Hanoi. Vingroup is one of the largest conglomerates of Vietnam, focusing on technology, industry, real estate development, retail, and services from healthcare to hospitality. As of 2022, Vingroup's revenue and that of its subsidiaries accounted for nearly 1.1% of Vietnam's GDP⠀⠀

about: Singapore-listed property group (SGX: C09), part of the Hong Leong Group controlled by Kwek Leng Beng, founded in 1963. Develops and owns residential condominiums, offices, malls and serviced apartments, and holds hotels through Millennium & Copthorne, with a portfolio spanning roughly 20 countries including the UK, Japan, China and Australia. Earns from property sales, rental income and hotel operations, and manages real estate funds. Billions in assets. Well known in Singapore for premium residential developments and the Millennium and Copthorne hotel brands, but B2B-style brand elsewhere.

wiki.title: City Developments Limited
wiki.text: City Developments Limited (CDL), sometimes also known as CityDev, is a Singaporean multinational real estate operating organisation. Founded in 1963, CDL first developed projects in Johor Bahru, Malaysia, as well as in Singapore. However, due to the racial and political situation in Singapore and Malaysia, CDL was forced to sell its properties in Johor Bahru and consolidate itself into the Singapore market. CDL came under the control of Hong Leong Bank via shares acquisition in 1969. Since then, CDL has developed numerous types of properties from shopping malls to integrated developments.

about: Somnigroup International is the Lexington, Kentucky mattress and bedding company formed when Tempur Sealy acquired Mattress Firm in 2025 and renamed itself. It makes and sells Tempur-Pedic, Sealy and Stearns & Foster mattresses and operates thousands of Mattress Firm retail stores in the US plus international markets, with revenue above $7 billion. Listed on the NYSE (SGI). Strong consumer brands; Tempur has long used sports and celebrity marketing.

wiki.title: Somnigroup International
wiki.text: Somnigroup International Inc. is an American manufacturer of mattresses and bedding products.

about: Kalyan Jewellers is one of India's largest jewellery retailers, selling gold, diamond and gemstone jewellery under the Kalyan and Candere brands through about 250 or more showrooms in India and the Middle East. Customers are consumers, especially for weddings and festivals, with revenue over INR 20,000 crore. Founded in 1993 and based in Thrissur, Kerala. Listed on NSE and BSE since 2021 (KALYANKJIL), backed by Warburg Pincus earlier. Very strong consumer brand in India, featuring celebrity ambassadors such as Amitabh Bachchan.

wiki.title: Kalyan Jewellers
wiki.text: Kalyan Jewellers is an Indian multinational jewellery company, headquartered in Thrissur, Kerala. It was founded in 1993 by T. S. Kalyanaraman. As of April 2026, Kalyan Jewellers operates 507 showrooms across India, Middle East and the US.

about: Global beauty company in fragrance, cosmetics and skincare, with brands such as CoverGirl, Rimmel, Sally Hansen, Max Factor, Gucci, Burberry, Calvin Klein and Hugo Boss licences. Sells to consumers through department stores, mass retailers and online, with revenue near 5.9 billion dollars. Legal seat in Amsterdam, with offices in New York and Paris; founded 1904. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (COTY), with JAB Holding a large shareholder. Strong consumer brands and licence brands with sports tie-ins.

wiki.title: Coty
wiki.text: Coty Inc. is a multinational beauty company founded in Paris in 1904 by François Coty. Today, the company is incorporated in Delaware, United States, with its global headquarters in Amsterdam, Netherlands. With its subsidiaries, it develops, manufactures, markets, and distributes fragrances, cosmetics, skin care, nail care, and both professional and retail hair care products. Coty owns around 40 brands as of 2024.

about: Prestige beauty company with brands including Estee Lauder, Clinique, MAC, La Mer, Bobbi Brown, Tom Ford Beauty, Jo Malone London, Aveda and Origins, selling skincare, makeup, fragrance and haircare in about 150 countries through department stores, travel retail and online. Revenue near 15 billion dollars. Headquartered in New York; founded 1946, still controlled by the Lauder family. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (EL). Very strong consumer brand, with Formula 1 and film partnerships.

wiki.title: Estée Lauder Companies
wiki.text: The Estée Lauder Companies Inc. is an American multinational cosmetics company, a manufacturer and marketer of makeup, skincare, perfume, and hair care products, based in Midtown Manhattan, New York City. It is the second largest cosmetics company in the world after L'Oréal. The company owns a diverse portfolio of brands, including La Mer, Jo Malone London, Clinique and Tom Ford Beauty, among many more, distributed internationally through both digital commerce and retail channels.

about: Shein is a Singapore-headquartered online fast-fashion retailer, founded in China by Chris Xu, selling inexpensive apparel, beauty, home goods and accessories directly to consumers in over 150 countries via its app and website, using a quick on-demand supply chain. Revenue is estimated near $30-40bn. Valued at about $66bn in 2023 and pursuing a London or Hong Kong listing. Private. Extremely high consumer awareness among younger shoppers, with active influencer marketing, though under scrutiny for labour and environmental practices.

wiki.title: Shein
wiki.text: Shein is a global e-commerce platform specializing in fast fashion. While the company primarily focuses on women's clothing, it also offers men's apparel, children's wear, accessories, cosmetics, shoes, bags, and other fashion items. Shein mainly focuses on Europe, Americas, Australia, and the Middle East along with other consumer markets worldwide.

about: e.l.f. Beauty is a US cosmetics and skincare company headquartered in Oakland, California and listed on the NYSE (ELF), with brands e.l.f. Cosmetics, e.l.f. SKIN, Naturium, Keys Soulcare and, from 2025, rhode. It sells affordable makeup through mass retailers such as Target, Walmart and Ulta and online, with annual net sales above 1.3 billion dollars. Founded 2004. Customers are Gen Z and millennial consumers. Strong consumer brand known for social media marketing and brand collaborations.

Moncler is an Italian luxury fashion house, headquartered in Milan and listed on Borsa Italiana (MONC), famous for its quilted down jackets. Under chairman and CEO Remo Ruffini, it sells ready-to-wear, accessories and outerwear through Moncler and Stone Island, which it bought in 2021, via its own stores, e-commerce and wholesale. Revenue is around 3 billion euros. Founded in 1952 in Monestier-de-Clermont, France. Highly visible luxury consumer brand worldwide.

wiki.title: Moncler
wiki.what: Italian luxury fashion house specializing in outerwear
wiki.text: Moncler S.p.A. is an Italian luxury fashion brand specialized in ready-to-wear outerwear headquartered in Milan, Italy. Its core branding includes the cockerel, "M" monogram, felt appliqué badge, crossed skis and cartoon duck mascot.

about: UK sports, premium and luxury retail group owning Sports Direct, House of Fraser, Flannels, Evans Cycles, GAME and Jack Wills, and holding minority stakes in other retailers such as ASOS and Boohoo. Customers are consumers via stores and online, with revenue near 5.5 billion pounds. Headquartered in Shirebrook, Derbyshire (input shows London); led by Mike Ashley. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (FRAS). Mass-market sports retail brand in the UK and Europe.

wiki.title: Frasers Group
wiki.what: British retail and real estate conglomerate
wiki.text: Frasers Group plc is a British retail, real estate, intellectual property and investment conglomerate, named after its ownership of the department store chain House of Fraser.

about: US house of fashion brands owning Coach, Kate Spade New York and Stuart Weitzman (sold to Caleres in 2025), selling handbags, accessories, footwear and apparel to consumers through its own stores, e-commerce, wholesale and outlets in about 40 countries. Revenue near 7 billion dollars. Headquartered in New York; founded 1941 as Coach. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (TPR). Its attempted acquisition of Capri Holdings was blocked in 2024. Strong consumer fashion brands.

wiki.title: Tapestry
wiki.what: Form of textile art, traditionally woven on a vertical loom
wiki.text: Tapestry is a form of textile art which was traditionally woven by hand on a loom. Normally it is used to create images rather than patterns. Tapestry is relatively fragile, and difficult to make, so most historical pieces are intended to hang vertically on a wall, or sometimes to lie horizontally over a piece of furniture such as a table or bed. Some periods made smaller pieces, often long and narrow and used as borders for other textiles. Most weavers use a natural warp thread, such as wool, linen, or cotton. The weft threads are usually wool or cotton but may include silk, gold, silver, or other alternatives.

wiki.title: Tapestry, Inc.
wiki.text: Tapestry, Inc. is an American holding company based in New York City which is the parent company of Coach New York and Kate Spade New York. Originally named Coach, Inc., the business changed its name to Tapestry on October 31, 2017.

about: Birkenstock Holding is a German footwear maker, headquartered in Linz am Rhein, known for contoured cork-footbed sandals such as the Arizona and Boston clog, and now a broad fashion and comfort shoe brand. It sells via wholesale, its own stores and e-commerce in over 100 countries, with revenue about EUR 2bn. Owned largely by L Catterton, the Gucci family-linked fund, after a 2021 deal, and listed on the NYSE (BIRK) since October 2023. Highly visible global consumer fashion brand, famed for the Barbie film tie-in.

wiki.title: Birkenstock
wiki.text: Birkenstock Holding plc is a German shoe manufacturer known for its sandals and other shoes notable for contoured cork footbeds (soles), made with layers of suede and jute, which conform to the shape of their wearers' feet. Founded in 1774 by Johann Adam Birkenstock and headquartered in Neustadt (Wied), Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany, the company's original purpose was to create shoes that support and contour the foot, compared to the flat soles of many shoes during that time. In 1896, the Fussbett (footbed) was designed, and by 1925, Birkenstocks were sold all over Europe.

about: JD Sports Fashion is a UK sports and fashion retailer based in Bury St Edmunds, operating JD, Size?, Footpatrol, Finish Line, Shoe Palace, Hibbett and Pretavous stores across Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific. It sells sneakers and apparel from Nike, Adidas and others, plus own-label products, through about 3,500 stores and e-commerce, with revenue near GBP 11bn. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (JD.). Strong youth consumer brand, active in sponsorship, including football clubs and the Premier League.

wiki.title: JD Sports
wiki.text: JD Sports Fashion plc, commonly known as JD Sports, JD or JD Group is a British multinational sports-fashion retail company based in Bury, Greater Manchester, England. It is listed on the London Stock Exchange and is a constituent of the FTSE 100 Index. The Pentland Group owns 55% of the company. The company operates mainly in Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific.

about: Golden Goose is a Milan-based Italian luxury footwear and fashion brand, famed for its pre-distressed hand-finished Super-Star sneakers, plus Ball Star, apparel and accessories, sold through boutiques, e-commerce and department stores in Europe, North America and Asia. Revenue is about EUR 600m. Owned by Permira, which bought it from Carlyle in 2020, with Hillhouse-led co-investors. Private, with a possible IPO. Strong luxury-fashion brand among younger affluent buyers.

wiki.title: The Golden Goose
wiki.text: "The Golden Goose" is a fairy tale collected by the Brothers Grimm.

wiki.title: Golden Goose (company)
wiki.text: Golden Goose (GG) is an Italian luxury fashion company specialized in footwear and apparel headquartered in Milan, Italy, by fashion designers Gallo and Rinaldo Founded in 2000 in Marghera near Venice, the brand is best known for its handcrafted sneakers with a distinctive distressed, vintage look. Its most recognizable model, the Super-Star, introduced in 2007, features a stylized star logo with one point deliberately shortened or obscured, reflecting the company's imperfect aesthetic.

about: Ralph Lauren is a New York luxury and lifestyle fashion company selling apparel, footwear, accessories, fragrance and home goods under Ralph Lauren Purple Label, Polo Ralph Lauren, Lauren and Double RL. It sells through wholesale, its own stores and e-commerce globally, with revenue near $7bn. Founder Ralph Lauren holds control. Listed on the NYSE (RL). Iconic consumer fashion brand, a long-time sports partner (US Open, Wimbledon, The Masters, Team USA), and visible across the sports and luxury market.

wiki.title: Ralph Lauren
wiki.text: Ralph Lauren is an American fashion designer, philanthropist, and billionaire businessman, best known for founding the brand Ralph Lauren, a global multibillion-dollar enterprise. He stepped down as CEO of the company in September 2015 but remains executive chairman and chief creative officer. As of June 2026, his net worth is estimated at US$15.2 billion.

about: Under Armour is a Baltimore-based sportswear company founded in 1996 by Kevin Plank, making performance apparel, footwear and accessories sold through wholesale, own stores and e-commerce in North America, EMEA and Asia-Pacific. Annual revenue is about $5 billion. Listed on NYSE (UAA, UA). Customers are athletes and sports consumers. Very high consumer brand awareness, with major sponsorship deals in athletics, college sports and golf.

wiki.title: Under Armour
wiki.what: American sports clothing and accessories company
wiki.text: Under Armour, Inc. is an American sportswear company that manufactures footwear and apparel headquartered in Baltimore, Maryland, United States.

about: Gap Inc. is a US apparel retailer headquartered in San Francisco and listed on the NYSE (GAP). It owns Gap, Old Navy, Banana Republic and Athleta, selling clothing and accessories through roughly 3,500 company-operated and franchise stores and online in the US and abroad, with annual revenue around 15 billion dollars. Customers are mainstream consumers; money comes from retail sales. Founded 1969. One of the most recognised fashion brands globally, with large consumer reach and marketing partnerships.

wiki.title: Gap Inc.
wiki.text: The Gap, Inc., commonly known as Gap Inc., headquartered in San Francisco, California, is an American multinational clothing and accessories retailer. The company operates four primary divisions: the namesake Gap, Banana Republic, Old Navy, and Athleta. Gap Inc. is one of the largest apparel retailers in the United States. It operates 3,569 stores. Zac Posen is the creative director of the Gap.

about: Levi Strauss & Co. is the US denim and apparel company headquartered in San Francisco and listed on the NYSE (LEVI). Its Levi's jeans, Dockers (sold in 2025 to Authentic Brands), Signature by Levi Strauss and Beyond Yoga brands are sold through wholesale, 3,000-plus own and franchised stores and online in over 100 countries, with revenue near 6 billion dollars. Founded 1853. Customers are mainstream consumers worldwide. One of the best-known apparel brands in the world with long sports and music marketing.

wiki.title: Levi Strauss & Co.
wiki.text: Levi Strauss & Co. is an American clothing company known worldwide for its Levi's brand of denim jeans. It was founded in May 1853 when German-Jewish immigrant Levi Strauss moved from New York City, New York, to San Francisco, California, to open a West Coast branch of his brothers' New York dry goods business. The corporation is registered in Delaware and its headquarters is located in Levi's Plaza in San Francisco.

about: LPP is a Polish fashion retail group based in Gdansk, owning the brands Reserved, Cropp, House, Mohito and Sinsay, sold through thousands of stores and online in Poland, Central and Eastern Europe, the Baltics, and expanding into Western Europe and the Middle East. Founded in 1991, it is listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange (LPP) with revenue above 4 billion euros. Strong consumer brands in Poland and the region.

wiki.title: LPP (company)
wiki.text: LPP S.A. is a Polish multinational fashion group headquartered in Gdańsk, Poland. The company specializes in the distribution of clothing, footwear, accessories, as well as home and pet products, offered under its own brands through an extensive network of brick-and-mortar stores and e-commerce channels. LPP owns five distinct fashion brands: Reserved, House, Cropp, Mohito, and Sinsay, each catering to different customer segments and style preferences. LPP currently operates on 41 global markets, continually expanding its international footprint and digital reach, and currently employs nearly 30,000 people in its offices, distribution network

about: Nike is the world's largest sportswear company, designing and selling footwear, apparel, equipment and accessories under Nike, Jordan and Converse, through retail stores, wholesale partners and digital channels. Founded in 1964 (as Blue Ribbon Sports) and headquartered in Beaverton, Oregon, it has revenue of about 46 billion dollars and around 78,000 employees. Listed on the NYSE (NKE). One of the most recognisable consumer brands globally, with large athlete endorsements and sponsorship deals in football, athletics, basketball and more.

wiki.title: Nike, Inc.
wiki.text: Nike, Inc. is an American athletic footwear and apparel corporation headquartered near Beaverton, Oregon. It is the world's largest supplier of athletic shoes and apparel and a major manufacturer of sports equipment, with revenue in excess of US$46 billion in its fiscal year 2022.

about: Li-Ning is a Chinese sportswear company, founded in 1990 by Olympic gymnast Li Ning, and headquartered in Beijing. It designs and sells sports apparel, footwear and equipment under Li-Ning, with badminton, running, basketball and lifestyle lines including China Li-Ning fashion. Listed in Hong Kong (2331) with revenue of about 27 billion yuan and thousands of stores. A very high awareness brand in China, with global sports sponsorships.

wiki.title: Li-Ning
wiki.text: Li-Ning Company Limited is a Chinese sportswear and sports equipment company founded by former Olympic gymnast Li Ning. The company endorses a number of international athletes and teams.

about: Kontoor Brands is a Greensboro, North Carolina apparel company spun off from VF Corporation in 2019, owning the Wrangler and Lee denim and lifestyle brands, sold through department stores, mass retailers, Western wear shops and its own channels in the US, Europe and Asia. Revenue is around US$2.6 billion. It is listed on the NYSE (KTB). Wrangler is a long-standing rodeo and country music partner. Strong consumer brands recognised globally, and an established sponsor, notably of Professional Bull Riders and events.

wiki.title: Kontoor Brands
wiki.text: Kontoor Brands is an American company that markets clothing under the Wrangler and Helly Hansen brands and operates VF Outlet.

about: Crocs is a US footwear company based in Broomfield, Colorado, and listed on Nasdaq (CROX). It sells the Crocs clog, sandals and Jibbitz charms, plus the HEYDUDE casual shoe brand, bought in 2022 for about 2.5 billion dollars. It sells through retailers, its own stores and websites in more than 85 countries, with revenue of around 4 billion dollars. Founded in 2002, it is a strong consumer brand known for celebrity and athlete collaborations.

wiki.title: Crocs
wiki.text: Crocs, Inc. is an American footwear company based in Broomfield, Colorado, which manufactures and markets the Crocs brand of foam footwear. Crocs, Inc. terms these "clogs", but they do not contain wood like traditional clogs. In 2021, they acquired the Italian footwear brand HEYDUDE for $2.5 billion. In 2025, Crocs revenue stood at $3.3 billion, an increase of 1.5% from the previous year.

about: Anheuser-Busch InBev is the world's largest brewer, headquartered in Leuven, Belgium, with brands including Budweiser, Corona, Stella Artois, Michelob Ultra, Beck's, Skol, Brahma and Modelo. It sells beer and soft drinks in over 150 countries, with revenue near $60bn and about 150,000 employees. Listed on Euronext Brussels (ABI), with secondary listings in Mexico, South Africa and the NYSE. A massive consumer portfolio and a long-time global sports sponsor, including the FIFA World Cup, F1 Budweiser partnerships and the Olympics.

wiki.title: AB InBev
wiki.what: Belgian multinational beverage and brewing company
wiki.text: Anheuser-Busch InBev SA/NV, known as AB InBev, is a Belgian multinational drink and brewing company based in Leuven, Belgium. It is the largest brewer in the world, and in 2023, was ranked 72nd in the Forbes Global 2000.

about: Bangkok-based Thai alcohol and beverage group, ThaiBev, owning Chang beer, Sangsom rum, Mekhong and Oishi food and drinks businesses. Controlled by the Charoen Sirivadhanabhakdi family and listed in Singapore. Strong Thai consumer brand and a well-known sports sponsor, including football clubs. Revenue is above THB 270 billion. ThaiBev employs about 40,000 people and exports to many Asian markets, and the group owns Fraser and Neave and the Oishi brand.

North American beverage company formed in 2018, combining Keurig Green Mountain coffee brewers and K-Cups with Dr Pepper Snapple's soft drinks, including Dr Pepper, 7UP, Canada Dry, Snapple, A&W and Core, and the acquisition of GHOST energy drinks. Sells to consumers through retailers and foodservice, with revenue near 15 billion dollars. Headquartered in Burlington, Massachusetts and Frisco, Texas. Listed on Nasdaq (KDP), with JAB Holding a major holder; it announced a 2025 plan to acquire JDE Peet's. Strong US consumer brands.

wiki.title: Keurig Dr Pepper
wiki.text: Keurig Dr Pepper, Inc. is an American drinks conglomerate with dual headquarters in Burlington, Massachusetts, and Frisco, Texas. The company was formed on July 9, 2018, through the merger of Keurig Green Mountain and Dr Pepper Snapple Group.

about: French hospitality group operating or franchising about 5,700 hotels in 110 countries under brands such as Sofitel, Pullman, Novotel, Mercure, Ibis, Fairmont, Raffles, Swissotel, Mövenpick and the Ennismore lifestyle brands, plus ALL loyalty and sport venue naming. Earns management and franchise fees. Headquartered in Issy-les-Moulineaux near Paris. Listed on Euronext Paris (AC), with Saudi PIF-linked Kingdom Holding a significant shareholder. Established consumer brands and an experienced sports sponsor, including Paris venue and football partnerships.

wiki.title: Accor
wiki.text: Accor S.A. is a French multinational hospitality company which owns, manages and franchises hotels, resorts and vacation properties. It is the largest hospitality company in Europe, and the sixth largest hospitality company worldwide.

about: Canadian convenience store and fuel retailer operating Circle K, Couche-Tard and Ingo, with around 17,000 stores in 29 countries across North America, Europe and Asia. Sells fuel, fast food and everyday items to consumers, with revenue near 70 billion dollars. Headquartered in Laval, Quebec; founded 1980. Listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (ATD). It pursued a 2025 bid for Seven & i, which later was withdrawn. Circle K is a very recognisable consumer brand and a past motorsport sponsor.

wiki.title: Couche-Tard
wiki.text: Alimentation Couche-Tard Inc., or simply Couche-Tard, is a Canadian multinational operator of convenience stores. The company operates approximately 16,700 stores across Canada, the United States, Mexico, Ireland, Norway, Sweden, Denmark, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland, Japan, Hong Kong, and Indonesia. The company operates its corporate stores mainly under the Couche-Tard, Circle K, and On the Run brands but also under the affiliated brands Mac's Convenience Stores, GetGo, go!, Provi-Soir, 7-jours, Dairy/Daisy Mart, Becker's and Winks.

about: French food and beverage group making dairy and plant-based products, specialised nutrition and water, with brands like Activia, Actimel, Alpro, Danonino, Evian, Volvic, Oikos, Silk and baby formula brands Aptamil and Nutricia. Sells to consumers through retail worldwide in more than 120 markets, with revenue near 27 billion euros and about 90,000 employees. Headquartered in Paris; founded 1919. Listed on Euronext Paris (BN). Very strong consumer brands and a regular sports sponsor (Evian and Volvic in sport).

wiki.title: Danone
wiki.text: Danone is a French multinational food-products corporation based in Paris. It was founded in 1919 in Barcelona, Spain. It is listed on Euronext Paris, where it is a component of the CAC 40 stock market index. In 2020, Danone became the first listed company to adopt the status of société à mission, as introduced by France's PACTE law of 2019.

about: Southeast Asia's leading super app, offering ride-hailing, food and grocery delivery (GrabFood), digital payments and financial services (GrabPay), across eight countries including Singapore, Indonesia, Malaysia and Vietnam. Earns commissions, advertising and financial fees, with about 40 million monthly users. Headquartered in Singapore; founded 2012 in Malaysia. Listed on Nasdaq (GRAB) since its 2021 SPAC merger. Strong consumer brand across Southeast Asia and a Formula 1 sponsor (Grab as a title sponsor of the Singapore Grand Prix).

wiki.title: Grab Holdings
wiki.text: Grab Holdings Inc. is a Singaporean multinational technology company headquartered in one-north, Singapore. It is the developer of a super-app for ride-hailing, food delivery, and digital payment services on mobile devices. It operates in Singapore, Malaysia, Cambodia, Indonesia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Thailand, and Vietnam.

about: British premium spirits and beer company owning Johnnie Walker, Smirnoff, Guinness, Tanqueray, Don Julio, Captain Morgan, Baileys and Crown Royal, sold in about 180 countries with revenue near 20 billion dollars. Customers are consumers via retailers, bars and restaurants and e-commerce. Headquartered in London; formed in 1997 from Guinness and Grand Metropolitan. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (DGE) and New York (DEO). Very strong consumer brands and a major sports sponsor, including Formula 1 as an official global Formula 1 partner through Johnnie Walker and Guinness 0.0.

wiki.title: Diageo
wiki.text: Diageo plc is a British multinational alcoholic beverage company headquartered in London, England. It operates from 110 sites in 180 countries. With brands such as Guinness, Johnnie Walker and Smirnoff, it is a major distributor of Scotch whisky and other spirits, with distilleries producing 40% of all Scotch whisky with over 24 brands. Diageo is a publicly traded company listed on both the London Stock Exchange where it is a constituent of the FTSE 100 Index, and the New York Stock Exchange as American depositary receipts.

about: One of the world's largest ice cream makers, producing brands under licence and in-house including Nestle brands under licence such as Drumstick and Maxibon, plus its own Mini Milk, Oreo and Cadbury ice cream licences and Cornetto-type novelties. Formed in 2016 as a joint venture of Nestle and PAI Partners. Sells to consumers through retailers in more than 20 countries, with revenue near 4 billion euros. Headquartered in Harrogate, North Yorkshire. Privately held. Corporate name little known; consumers know the product brands.

wiki.title: Froneri
wiki.text: Froneri International Limited is a British ice cream manufacturer with its headquarters in Leeming Bar, North Yorkshire, England. It is the second-largest producer of ice cream in the world by retail sales, after The Magnum Ice Cream Company, with the two companies together accounting for approximately 32% of total global retail sales.

about: The Magnum Ice Cream Company was demerged from Unilever in December 2025, owning Magnum, Wall's, Ben & Jerry's, Cornetto, Algida, Klondike, Breyers and Talenti, selling frozen desserts to consumers through retailers and freezers in about 100 countries. Revenue near 8 billion euros. Headquartered in Amsterdam. Listed in Amsterdam, London and New York. Very strong consumer ice cream brands.
cb_desc: The Magnum lce Cream Company is an ice cream...

wiki.title: The Magnum Ice Cream Company
wiki.text: The Magnum Ice Cream Company N.V. is a Dutch multinational ice cream company headquartered in Amsterdam, Netherlands. Incorporating several major ice cream brands and having about 21% of global market share, the Magnum Ice Cream Company is the world's largest ice cream manufacturer. The Magnum Ice Cream Company formed on 1 July 2025 as an independent subsidiary of Unilever, encompassing Unilever's ice cream division. In December 2025, the subsidiary was separated and admitted to the regulated markets of publicly listed shares on Euronext Amsterdam, London Stock Exchange, and New York Stock Exchange.

about: US restaurant franchise operator with KFC, Taco Bell, Pizza Hut and The Habit Burger & Grill, with over 60,000 restaurants in more than 155 countries and a heavily franchised model that earns royalties. Revenue near 7.5 billion dollars. Headquartered in Louisville, Kentucky; spun off from PepsiCo in 1997. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (YUM). Separate Yum China is a listed entity. Very strong consumer fast-food brands and long-standing sports sponsors, including Taco Bell's links with motorsport.

wiki.title: Yum! Brands
wiki.text: Yum! Brands, Inc. is an American multinational fast food corporation. Based in Louisville, Kentucky, the company operates KFC, Taco Bell, Habit Burger & Grill, and several technology companies. As of 2024 Yum! is the world's second largest fast food restaurant chain by gross revenues, after McDonald's, though the large majority of Yum! locations are independently owned franchises and the parent company's revenue is substantially lower than gross revenues.

about: Grupo Nutresa is a Colombian processed food group making cold cuts, chocolates, biscuits, coffee, ice cream (Helados Crem Helado) and pasta, with brands such as Colcafe, Noel, Zenu and Jet. Customers are consumers across Latin America, with revenue near 3 billion dollars. Headquartered in Medellin. Controlled since 2025 by the Gilinski family's Nugil, which took control from Grupo Sura and Argos in a takeover. Trades on the Colombian Stock Exchange (NUTRESA). Strong Colombian consumer brands.

wiki.title: Grupo Nutresa
wiki.text: Grupo Nutresa S.A. (in English: Nutresa Group), formerly Grupo Nacional de Chocolates S.A. (in English: Chocolate National Group S.A.), is a Colombian multinational food processing conglomerate headquartered in Medellín. The group's principal activities are producing, distributing, and selling cold cuts, biscuits, chocolates, coffee, ice cream and pasta. The company markets its products under approximately 70 different brands in 65 countries. Other activities include the investment or application of resources or cash under whatever form authorized by law and the exploration of the metal-mechanic and packaging industry. In 2004, the group bega

about: Constellation Brands is a US beverage alcohol company best known for imported Mexican beers (Corona, Modelo, Pacifico) which it brews for the US market, plus wine and spirits such as Robert Mondavi, Meiomi and Casa Noble (Kim Crawford sold in 2024). Revenue near 10 billion dollars. Headquartered in Victor, New York (input shows Rochester). Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (STZ). Very strong beer brands and a long-time sponsor of sports including UFC, boxing and motorsport.

wiki.title: Constellation Brands
wiki.text: Constellation Brands, Inc. is an American producer and marketer of beer, wine, and spirits. A Fortune 500 company, Constellation is the largest beer import company in the US, measured by sales, and has the third-largest market share of all major beer suppliers. It also has sizable investments in medical and recreational cannabis through its association with Canopy Growth. Based in Rochester, New York, Constellation has about 40 facilities and approximately 9,000 employees.

about: McCormick & Company is a US spice, seasoning and flavour company, owning McCormick, Frank's RedHot, French's, Cholula, Old Bay, Lawry's, Schwartz, Club House and Ducros, plus flavour solutions sold to food manufacturers and restaurants. Revenue near 6.7 billion dollars. Headquartered in Hunt Valley, Maryland (Sparks); founded 1889. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (MKC). Strong consumer pantry brands, with some sports partnerships.

wiki.title: McCormick & Company
wiki.what: American spice, herb, and flavoring provider
wiki.text: McCormick & Company, Incorporated is an American food company that manufactures, markets, and distributes spices, seasoning mixes, condiments, and other flavoring products to retail outlets, food manufacturers, and food service businesses.

about: Mondelez International is a global snacking group, with Oreo, Cadbury, Milka, Toblerone, Ritz, Chips Ahoy, Trident, Halls and Sour Patch Kids, sold in more than 150 countries. Revenue near 38 billion dollars and about 90,000 employees. Headquartered in Chicago, Illinois; spun off from Kraft Foods in 2012. Listed on Nasdaq (MDLZ). Very strong consumer brands and an active sports and events sponsor, including Olympic and football partnerships.

wiki.title: Mondelez International
wiki.what: American multinational food and beverage corporation
wiki.text: Mondelez International, Inc. is an American multinational confectionery, food, holding, beverage, and snack food company based in Chicago. Mondelez has an annual revenue of about $38.5 billion and operates in approximately 160 countries. It ranked No. 108 in the 2021 Fortune 500 list of the largest United States corporations by total revenue.

about: Subway is one of the world's largest restaurant franchises, with about 37,000 locations in over 100 countries, selling made-to-order sandwiches, salads and wraps. Based in Milford, Connecticut, though Crunchbase lists a Canadian address. Operations are overwhelmingly franchised, earning royalties and fees from franchisees. In 2024 it was acquired by Roark Capital for about $9.6bn, taking over from founders' families. Private. Extremely high global consumer brand awareness and a regular sports sponsor and advertiser.

wiki.title: Subway (restaurant)
wiki.text: Subway IP LLC, trading as Subway, is an American multinational fast food restaurant franchise that specializes in submarine sandwiches (subs) and wraps. It was founded by Fred DeLuca and financed by Peter Buck in 1965 as Pete's Super Submarine Sandwiches in Bridgeport, Connecticut. After several name changes, it was renamed Subway in 1972, and a franchise operation began in 1974 with a second restaurant in Wallingford, Connecticut.

about: Carrefour is a French multinational retail group, based in Massy, running hypermarkets, supermarkets, convenience stores, cash-and-carry and e-commerce in France, Spain, Italy, Belgium, Brazil, Argentina and other countries, with about 14,000 stores, 300,000+ staff and revenue of roughly EUR 90bn. It earns from grocery and non-food sales, plus banking, insurance and retail media. Listed on Euronext Paris (CA); the Moulin family via Galfa and Peninsula Europe are key shareholders. Very strong consumer brand, a long-time sponsor of sport such as the Tour de France and French football.

wiki.title: Carrefour
wiki.what: French multinational retail and wholesaling corporation
wiki.text: Carrefour Group, S.A. is a French multinational retail and wholesaling corporation headquartered in Massy, France. It operates a chain of hypermarkets, grocery stores and convenience stores. By 2024, the group had 14,000 stores in 40 countries. It is the seventh-largest retailer in the world by revenue.

about: MBRF is the Brazilian food group formed in 2025 by the merger of Marfrig and BRF, headquartered in Sao Paulo. Its brands include Sadia, Perdigao, Qualy, Bassi and Marfrig, covering beef, chicken, pork, processed and plant-based foods, selling in Brazil and over 140 countries, with revenue above BRL 150bn and a workforce of about 150,000. Listed on B3 (MBRF3). Strong consumer brands in Brazil, and Sadia and Perdigao have a long history of football sponsorship.

Molson Coors is a Chicago-based global brewer, with brands Coors Light, Miller Lite, Molson Canadian, Blue Moon, Carling, Staropramen and Madri, selling in the US, Canada, Europe and other markets, with revenue near $11bn and about 16,000 employees. It also has a growing non-beer beverage portfolio. Listed on the NYSE (TAP). Very strong consumer brands, and a heavy long-running sports sponsor, including NHL, NFL and soccer.

wiki.title: Molson Coors
wiki.text: Molson Coors Beverage Company is a Canadian-American multinational drink and brewing company. The company is the fifth-largest brewer worldwide by beer output. Its operational headquarters are in Chicago with offices in Prague for the EMEA division and in Golden, Colorado for its US division and Montréal, Québec for its Canadian division.

about: General Mills is a Minneapolis-based global packaged food company with brands such as Cheerios, Nature Valley, Haagen-Dazs, Pillsbury, Betty Crocker, Yoplait, Old El Paso, Blue Buffalo pet food and Annie's. It sells through grocery and foodservice channels in more than 100 countries, with revenue near $19bn and about 34,000 employees. Listed on the NYSE (GIS). Highly recognised consumer brands in North America and abroad, with large advertising budgets and sports sponsorships.

wiki.title: General Mills
wiki.text: General Mills, Inc. is an American multinational manufacturer and marketer of branded consumer foods sold through retail stores. Founded on the banks of the Mississippi River at Saint Anthony Falls in Minneapolis, the company originally gained fame for being a large flour miller. It is headquartered in Golden Valley, Minnesota, a suburb of Minneapolis.

about: Domino's Pizza is an Ann Arbor, Michigan pizza chain with over 21,000 stores in more than 90 countries, mostly franchised, including delivery and carry-out, with strong digital ordering. System-wide sales are above $19bn. Master franchisees such as Domino's Pizza Enterprises (Australia) and DP Eurasia operate abroad. Listed on the NYSE (DPZ). Very high consumer brand awareness, with big advertising spend and sports sponsorships, such as NASCAR and MLS.

wiki.title: Domino's
wiki.text: Domino's Pizza, Inc., trading as Domino's, is an American multinational pizza restaurant chain founded in 1960. The corporation is Delaware-domiciled and headquartered at the Domino's Farms office park in Ann Arbor Township near Ann Arbor, Michigan. As of 2018, Domino's had approximately 15,000 stores, with 5,649 in the United States, 1,500 in India, and 1,249 in the United Kingdom. Domino's has stores in more than 83 countries and 5,701 cities worldwide.

about: Coca-Cola FEMSA is a Mexico City-based beverage company, the world's largest franchise bottler of Coca-Cola products, serving Mexico, Brazil, Colombia, Argentina and other Latin American countries, with over 250 million consumers and 3.9 billion unit cases sold. Owned partly by FEMSA and The Coca-Cola Company, it is listed on the Mexican exchange (KOF UBL) and NYSE (KOF). Customers are retailers, restaurants and consumers. Strong visibility via Coca-Cola brands, including sponsorship activity.

wiki.title: Coca-Cola FEMSA
wiki.text: Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V., known as Coca-Cola FEMSA or KOF, is a Mexican multinational beverage company headquartered in Mexico City, Mexico. It is a subsidiary of FEMSA which owns 47.8% of its stock, with 27.8% held by wholly owned subsidiaries of The Coca-Cola Company and the remaining 25% listed publicly on the Mexican Stock Exchange and the New York Stock Exchange. It is the largest franchise Coca-Cola bottler in the world, the company has operations in Latin America, although its largest and most profitable market is in Mexico.

about: Luckin Coffee is a Xiamen, China-based coffee chain, founded in 2017, with more than 24,000 stores in China, selling coffee, tea and snacks mostly through a mobile app for pickup and delivery. It overtook Starbucks in China store count. After a 2020 accounting fraud scandal it was delisted from Nasdaq, restructured and traded over the counter, and is controlled by Centurium Capital. Very high consumer brand awareness in China, with global expansion into Singapore and the US starting.

wiki.title: Luckin Coffee
wiki.text: Luckin Coffee Inc. (Chinese: 瑞幸咖啡; pinyin: Ruìxìng Kāfēi) is a Chinese coffee company and coffeehouse chain founded in Beijing in 2017. In the first half of 2026, Luckin had 35,000 stores globally. The company operates shops, stores, and kiosks that offer coffee, tea, and food, generally at lower prices than their competitors. Purchases can only be made using an online app. Luckin is headquartered in Xiamen, Fujian. The company has expanded rapidly since its founding, and by 2019, its stores outnumbered Starbucks locations in China. In 2020, short-seller Carson Block and his firm Muddy Waters Research published an anonymous 89-page investigat

about: Tesco is the UK's largest supermarket group, headquartered in Welwyn Garden City, Hertfordshire and listed on the LSE (TSCO). It operates thousands of Tesco, Express and Extra stores plus Booker wholesale, Clubcard loyalty and Tesco Bank (now largely sold), with operations in Ireland and Central Europe, 330,000 employees and revenue over 68 billion pounds. Founded 1919. Customers are mainstream shoppers. Hugely recognisable consumer brand with prior sponsorships in sport and charity.

wiki.title: Tesco
wiki.text: Tesco PLC is a British multinational groceries and general merchandise retailer headquartered in the United Kingdom at its head offices in Welwyn Garden City, England. The company was founded by Sir Jack Cohen in Hackney, London, in 1919. In 2023, it was the 15th largest retailer in the world by revenue. It is the market leader of groceries in the UK. Tesco also has stores in the Czech Republic, Ireland, Slovakia, the Isle of Man and Hungary.

about: Starbucks is the world's largest coffee chain, headquartered in Seattle, Washington and listed on Nasdaq (SBUX). It operates about 40,000 company-owned and licensed stores in over 80 countries, selling coffee, tea, food and packaged goods, with about 380,000 employees and revenue near 36 billion dollars. Founded 1971. Customers are mainstream consumers; also earns from Nestle licensing of packaged products. One of the most recognised consumer brands globally with loyalty programme and heavy marketing.

wiki.title: Starbucks
wiki.text: Starbucks Corporation is an American multinational chain of coffeehouses and roastery reserves headquartered in Seattle, Washington. It was founded in 1971 by Jerry Baldwin, Zev Siegl, and Gordon Bowker at Seattle's Pike Place Market initially as a coffee bean wholesaler. Starbucks was converted into a coffee shop serving espresso-based drinks under the ownership of Howard Schultz, who was chief executive officer from 1986 to 2000 and led the aggressive expansion of the franchise across the West Coast of the United States.

about: Milan-based Italian spirits company, founded 1860, owning Aperol, Campari, Wild Turkey, Skyy, Grand Marnier and Appleton Estate, sold in about 190 countries with revenue near EUR 3.1 billion. Listed in Milan (CPR). Strong consumer brand, especially in cocktails, with Aperol Spritz a global trend; active in motorsport and sports sponsorship. Campari employs about 5,000 people and has a large presence in Italy, the US, Brazil and Jamaica.

wiki.title: Campari Group
wiki.text: Davide Campari-Milano N.V., trading as Campari Group, is an Italian company active since 1860 in the branded beverage industry. It produces spirits, wines, and non-alcoholic apéritifs. From its signature product, Campari, its portfolio has been extended to include over 50 brands, including Aperol, Appleton, Picon, SKYY vodka, Espolón, Wild Turkey, Grand Marnier, and Forty Creek whisky.

about: Dutch retail group formed by the 2016 merger of Ahold and Delhaize, owning Albert Heijn, Delhaize, Food Lion, Giant and Stop & Shop, with roughly 7,500 stores in Europe and the US and revenue of about EUR 90 billion. Headquartered in Zaandam and listed on Euronext Amsterdam (AD). Very high consumer visibility in its home markets, mostly local brands. Ahold Delhaize serves around 60 million customers weekly and employs roughly 400,000 people, and it sells grocery e-commerce under many local banners.

wiki.title: Ahold Delhaize
wiki.what: Dutch multinational retail and wholesaling company
wiki.text: Koninklijke Ahold Delhaize N.V., commonly known as Ahold Delhaize, is a Dutch multinational retail and wholesale holding company. Its name comes from the 2016 merger of two companies: Ahold (Dutch) and Delhaize Group (Belgian), which both have origins in the 1800s. Its business format includes supermarkets, convenience stores, hypermarkets, online grocery, online non-food, pharmacies, and liquor stores. Its 16 local brands employ 402,000 people at 7,716 stores across nine countries. The United States is where two-thirds of the holding company's revenue is generated.

about: Fast-casual Mexican restaurant chain founded in Denver in 1993 and now headquartered in Newport Beach, California, with about 3,900 restaurants mainly in the US plus Canada, the UK, France and Germany. Revenue is about $11 billion and it employs about 130,000 people. Listed on the NYSE (CMG). Very strong US consumer brand, now expanding internationally and sponsoring sport. Chipotle's menu is built around burritos, bowls and tacos, with ingredients it describes as responsibly sourced, and digital orders make up a large share of sales.

wiki.title: Chipotle Mexican Grill
wiki.text: Chipotle Mexican Grill, Inc., also known simply as Chipotle, is an American multinational chain of fast casual restaurants specializing in bowls, tacos, and Mission burritos made to order in front of the customer. As of December 2025, Chipotle has 4,000 locations. Its name derives from chipotle, the Nahuatl name for a smoked and dried jalapeño chili pepper.

about: Restaurant Brands International is the parent of fast-food chains Burger King, Tim Hortons, Popeyes and Firehouse Subs, plus the Carrefour-licensed Burger King and Tim Hortons international franchising operations. It earns royalties and rent from franchisees across more than 120 countries and over 30,000 restaurants, with system sales above 40 billion dollars. Created in 2014 when Burger King merged with Tim Hortons, backed by 3G Capital and Berkshire Hathaway; headquartered in Toronto and listed on the NYSE and TSX (QSR). Massive global consumer brands that already do large sports and entertainment marketing.

wiki.title: Restaurant Brands International
wiki.what: Canadian multinational fast food holding corporation
wiki.text: Restaurant Brands International Inc. (RBI) is a Canadian-based multinational fast food holding company. It was formed in 2014 by the $12.5 billion merger between American fast food restaurant chain Burger King and Canadian coffee shop and fast food restaurant chain Tim Hortons, and expanded by the purchases of Popeyes and Firehouse Subs in 2017 and 2021, respectively. The company is the fifth-largest operator of fast food restaurants in the world after Subway, McDonald's, Starbucks and Yum! Brands. They are based alongside Tim Hortons in Toronto (previously Oakville, Ontario). Burger King, Popeyes, and Firehouse Subs retain their existing ope

about: Compass Group is the world's largest contract catering company, headquartered in Chertsey, UK and listed on the London Stock Exchange (CPG). It runs restaurants and food services for businesses, schools, hospitals, sports venues, defence sites and offices across around 30 countries, through brands such as Levy and Eurest, with revenue of about 40 billion pounds and more than 500,000 employees. Levy provides hospitality at major sporting events. B2B brand with low consumer recognition, but strong in event hospitality.

wiki.title: Compass Group
wiki.text: Compass Group plc is a British multinational contract foodservice company headquartered in Chertsey, England. It is the largest contract foodservice company in Europe, employing over 590,000 people as of September 2025. It serves meals in locations including offices and factories, schools, universities, hospitals, major sports and cultural venues, mining camps, prisons and offshore oil platforms. Compass Group is listed on the London Stock Exchange, as a constituent of the FTSE 100 Index. As of July 2025, it has one of the highest market capitalisations on the London Stock Exchange. It is also a Fortune Global 500 company.

about: Ferrero is an Italian-founded confectionery group, with its holding in Luxembourg and operational base in Alba, Italy and Arlon. It makes Nutella, Kinder, Ferrero Rocher, Tic Tac and Raffaello and acquired Nestle's US candy business and Kellogg's cookies. Revenue is about 18 billion euros, from around 170 countries. Privately held by the Ferrero family. Extremely strong consumer brand, and active in sports sponsorship.

wiki.title: Ferrero SpA
wiki.text: Ferrero SpA ( fə-RAIR-oh, Italian: [ferˈrɛːro]), more commonly known as Ferrero Group or simply Ferrero, is an Italian multinational company with headquarters in Alba, Piedmont. Ferrero is a manufacturer of branded chocolate and confectionery products, and is reportedly the second largest chocolate producer and confectionery company in the world. Ferrero SpA is a private company owned by the Ferrero family and it has been described as "one of the world's most secretive firms". It was founded in 1946 in Alba by Pietro Ferrero, a confectioner and small-time pastry maker who laid the groundwork for the introduction of Nutella. The company had a

about: Marfrig is a Sao Paulo-based Brazilian meat processor, listed on B3 (MRFG3), which produces beef, lamb and plant-based products and is a major supplier to restaurant chains such as McDonald's and to supermarkets. It merged with BRF in 2025 to create MBRF. It is also a stakeholder in National Beef in the US. Funding shown is about $535 million. Consumer-facing brands are largely through its business partners.

wiki.title: Marfrig
wiki.text: Marfrig S.A. is the second largest Brazilian food processing company, after JBS. The company is headquartered in São Paulo. The company has 33 production units around the world and operational bases in 22 countries, exporting their products to over 100. Its activities include the production, processing, industrialization, sale and distribution of food based on animal protein, in addition to the sale of other food byproducts, such as frozen vegetables, sauces and desserts. The company is one of the largest beef producers in the world.

about: Elior Group is a French contract catering and services company based in La Defense, Paris, serving businesses, schools, hospitals, care homes and leisure sites in France, the UK, Spain, Italy and the US, including Elior Restauration and Elior Services. It earns revenue from meals and facility services under long contracts. Annual revenue is about 6 billion euros and it is listed on Euronext Paris (ELIOR). Visible to consumers in canteens and venues but weak as a standalone brand.

wiki.title: Elior Group
wiki.text: Elior Group is a multinational company that specializes in catering and food service. Based in France, Elior provides meal services to a variety of sectors including education, healthcare, business, and the travel sector, among others. The company operates primarily in Europe and the United States, offering both onsite dining and meal delivery services. They are also involved in facility management services through subsidiary companies.

about: Swire Pacific is a Hong Kong conglomerate, part of the Swire group, with interests in property (Pacific Place and Taikoo Place), aviation (Cathay Pacific stake, HAECO), beverages (Coca-Cola bottling in China and the US) and trading and industrial businesses. Operating mainly in Hong Kong, Mainland China and Southeast Asia, it is listed in Hong Kong (19 and 87) and controlled by John Swire & Sons. The Cathay Pacific and Coca-Cola bottler ties give it major visibility, with a history of sports sponsorship in the region.

wiki.title: Swire
wiki.text: Swire Group (Chinese: 太古集團) is a highly diversified global conglomerate with its parent company being John Swire & Sons Limited that holds controlling stakes in a range of businesses trading in the UK, USA, Australia, Papua New Guinea, East and West Africa, and across Southeast Asia. The Group's businesses are arranged into groups: property, aviation, beverages and food chain, marine services, and trading and industrial. Its core businesses are mainly focused on Asia, with its key operations in Hong Kong and mainland China. Within Asia, Swire's activities come under the group's publicly quoted arm, Swire Pacific Limited, which is the largest

about: Woolworths Group is Australia's largest retailer, operating Woolworths supermarkets, Metro Food Stores, BIG W discount department stores and Petstock, plus the Woolworths Rewards loyalty scheme, and in New Zealand it runs Countdown, rebranded Woolworths NZ. It has well over 1,000 stores and about 200,000 employees, with revenue near 67 billion Australian dollars. Headquartered in Bella Vista, Sydney, and listed on the ASX (WOW). Dominant mass-market grocery brand in Australia with huge consumer visibility and long-running sponsorship programmes.

wiki.title: Woolworths Group
wiki.text: Woolworths Group Limited is an Australian multinational retail and financial services company, currently headquartered in Bella Vista, New South Wales, a suburb of Sydney. The group operates the Woolworths supermarket chain in Australia and New Zealand, as well as the smaller Woolworths Metro chain. The group operates the Big W discount department store chain in Australia. In New Zealand, the group operates the SuperValue and FreshChoice supermarkets. The group also owns the Everyday Rewards program, serving both Australia and New Zealand. The company and its operations are named in tribute to the original Woolworth business in the United Sta

about: Brinker International is the Dallas-based owner and franchisor of the Chili's Grill & Bar and Maggiano's Little Italy restaurant brands, operating more than 1,600 restaurants, mainly in the US, with some franchised locations in about 30 countries. Revenue exceeds 4.5 billion dollars with about 100,000 employees. It also operates virtual brands such as It's Just Wings. Listed on the NYSE (EAT). Highly visible US casual dining brand, Chili's has been successful with social media marketing and value menus.

wiki.title: Brinker International
wiki.text: Brinker International, Inc. (or simply Brinker) is an American multinational hospitality industry company that owns Chili's and Maggiano's Little Italy restaurant chains. Founded in 1975 and based in Dallas, Texas, Brinker currently owns, operates, or franchises 1,672 restaurants under the names Chili's Grill & Bar and Maggiano's Little Italy worldwide.

about: Lamb Weston is one of the world's largest producers of frozen potato products, supplying french fries, hash browns, potato wedges and sweet potato items to restaurants, quick-service chains, retailers and foodservice, including McDonald's among large customers. It was spun off from Conagra Brands in 2016 and is headquartered in Eagle, Idaho, with European operations in Breda, Netherlands. Revenue is about 6.5 billion dollars, with listing on the NYSE (LW). B2B food brand, though its retail brand is Grown in Idaho.

wiki.title: Lamb Weston
wiki.text: Lamb Weston Holdings, Inc. is an American food processing company that is one of the world's largest producers and processors of frozen french fries, waffle fries, and other frozen potato products. It is headquartered in Eagle, Idaho, a suburb of Boise.

about: Coca-Cola Icecek (CCI) is a Turkish bottler of Coca-Cola Company beverages with operations in Turkey, Pakistan, Kazakhstan, Iraq, Egypt, Central Asia and elsewhere, producing and distributing sparkling drinks, juices, water and tea. Headquartered in Istanbul and listed on Borsa Istanbul (CCOLA), it is owned by Anadolu Group and the Coca-Cola Company. It sells Coca-Cola, Fanta, Sprite and Cappy. Revenue is around 3 billion dollars. Sells branded drinks with very high consumer visibility, though the bottler name is B2B.

wiki.title: Coca-Cola İçecek
wiki.what: Anchor bottler and a part of the Coca-Cola System
wiki.text: Coca-Cola İçecek A.Ş. is an anchor bottler and a part of the Coca-Cola System. It is 50.3% owned by Anadolu Efes, 20.1% owned by The Coca-Cola Company, 3.7% owned by Özgörkey Holding, and the remaining 25.9% publicly traded on the Borsa İstanbul (BIST). It is the 5th largest bottler in the Coca-Cola System in terms of sales volume. The company is headquartered in Istanbul. The company operates thirty factories in eleven countries, bottling Coca-Cola products in Azerbaijan, Iraq, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Syria, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, Bangladesh, and Jordan, as well as its home country of Turkey. The company is included

about: Mixue Bingcheng, known as Mixue Ice Cream and Tea, is a Zhengzhou, Henan, Chinese beverage and ice cream chain with over 40,000 mostly franchised stores in China and across Asia, selling cheap soft-serve ice cream, bubble tea and lemonade. It makes money by supplying franchisees with ingredients and equipment. Founded in 1997, it listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (2097) in 2025. A massive consumer brand in China, and increasingly in Southeast Asia, with the snow king mascot.

Minerva Foods is a South American meat processor headquartered in Barretos, Sao Paulo, Brazil. It slaughters and sells beef, as well as lamb, pork and by-products, with plants across Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Paraguay and Colombia, and exports to more than 100 countries. Customers are retailers, food service and importers, and it is one of the region's largest beef exporters. It is listed on Brazil's B3 exchange (BEEF3), controlled by the Vilela de Queiroz family. Mostly a B2B brand with limited consumer visibility.

wiki.title: Minerva Foods
wiki.text: Minerva Foods is a Brazilian food company founded in 1924 in the city of Barretos, São Paulo. The company is specializes in the trading of fresh beef, leather, derivatives, and the export of live cattle, as well as meat processing. It is the second-largest beef company in Brazil and Uruguay and the largest beef exporter in Paraguay, Colombia, and Argentina. It sells its products in over 100 countries. Minerva operates 26 slaughter and deboning plants (11 in Brazil, 3 in Paraguay, 4 in Uruguay, 1 in Colombia, and 5 in Argentina) and 3 processing plants, with a daily capacity to slaughter and debone approximately 54,000 heads of cattle.

about: Olam is a Singapore-headquartered agri-business that sources, processes and supplies food ingredients, spices, vegetables, coffee, cocoa, edible nuts and other agricultural products, now organised mainly into ofi (Olam Food Ingredients) and Olam Agri. Crunchbase's text refers to its spices and vegetable ingredients business, including dehydrated onion. Customers are global food and beverage makers and traders. Founded in 1989, it operates across dozens of countries and is controlled by Temasek-linked shareholders and listed in Singapore. Mostly B2B, with limited consumer brand visibility.

about: GRUMA is a Mexican food manufacturer based in Garza Garcia, Nuevo Leon, and the world's leading producer of corn flour and tortillas, with the Maseca and Mission brands plus Guerrero. It operates plants in North America, Europe, Asia and Oceania, selling to supermarkets, restaurants and foodservice, with revenue near US$7 billion. It is listed on the Mexican Stock Exchange (GRUMAB) and controlled by the Gonzalez family. Mission tortillas are widely recognised in the US and the group has sports sponsorship ties, such as football in Mexico.

wiki.title: Gruma
wiki.what: Mexican multinational corn flour (masa) and tortilla manufacturing company
wiki.text: Gruma, S.A.B. de C.V., known as Gruma, is a Mexican multinational corn flour (masa) and tortilla manufacturing company headquartered in San Pedro, near Monterrey, Nuevo León, Mexico. It is the largest corn flour and tortilla manufacturer in the world. Its brand names include Mission Foods (Misión in Mexico), Maseca, and Guerrero. Gruma reported revenues of US$3.8 billion for 2014. It operates more than 79 plants worldwide, mainly in Mexico, the United States, and Europe, and employs approximately 18,000 people. It is listed on the Mexican Stock Exchange since 1994, and it had a NYSE listing through ADRs from 1998 to September 2015. It is a co

about: Haidilao is a Chinese hot pot restaurant chain founded in Sichuan in 1994, known for table-side noodle-pulling, attentive service and free extras. Its holding company in Beijing is listed in Hong Kong (6862). It operates more than 1,300 restaurants in mainland China and abroad in Asia, North America, Europe and Australia, with annual revenue in the tens of billions of yuan. Haidilao is a very high-profile consumer brand in China and well known among Asian diaspora, and it has done sponsorship and partnerships.

Coca-Cola HBC is the second largest bottler of Coca-Cola products by volume, producing and distributing Coca-Cola, Fanta, Sprite, Monster, Costa Coffee and Finlandia in 29 countries across Europe, Eastern Europe and Africa. Revenue near 10 billion euros. Headquartered in Zug, Switzerland, with operational roots in Greece; Coca-Cola Company and Kar-Tess Holding are major shareholders. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (CCH) and Athens. B2B bottler that operates well-known Coca-Cola brands.

wiki.title: Coca-Cola HBC
wiki.text: Coca-Cola HBC AG, formerly known as Coca-Cola Hellenic Bottling Company or just Coca-Cola Hellenic, is the world's third-largest Coca-Cola anchor bottler in terms of volume with sales of more than 2 billion unit cases. Coca-Cola HBC's shares are primarily listed on the London Stock Exchange with a secondary listing on the Athens Stock Exchange. The company is a constituent of the FTSE 100 Index. Coca-Cola HBC has been named the industry leader among beverage companies in the 2014 Dow Jones Sustainability Index and is also included in the FTSE4Good Index.

about: Kimberly-Clark is a US consumer products company making Huggies diapers, Kleenex tissues, Cottonelle, Scott, Kotex and Depend, plus Kimberly-Clark Professional products, sold in 175 countries. Revenue near 20 billion dollars. Headquartered in Irving, Texas; founded 1872. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (KMB). In November 2025 it agreed to acquire Kenvue (Tylenol, Neutrogena) in a deal valued at around 48.7 billion dollars. Strongly visible household brands with a history of sports tie-ins.

wiki.title: Kimberly-Clark
wiki.text: Kimberly-Clark Corporation is an American multinational consumer goods and personal care corporation that produces mostly paper-based consumer products. The company manufactures sanitary paper products and surgical & medical instruments. Kimberly-Clark brand name products include Kleenex facial tissue, Kotex feminine hygiene products, Cottonelle, Scott and Andrex toilet paper, Wypall utility wipes, KimWipes scientific cleaning wipes and Huggies disposable diapers and baby wipes. Founded in Neenah, Wisconsin, in 1872 and based in the Las Colinas section of Irving, Texas, since 1985, the company operated its own paper mills around the world for

about: Wayfair is a US online retailer of home furnishings, decor and housewares, with Wayfair, Joss & Main, AllModern, Birch Lane and Perigold, offering several million products and opening physical stores. Revenue near 12 billion dollars and about 20 million active customers. Headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts; founded 2002. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (W). Strong consumer e-commerce brand with heavy performance marketing and occasional sports sponsorships.

wiki.title: Wayfair
wiki.text: Wayfair Inc. is an American multinational e-commerce company based in Boston, Massachusetts that sells furniture and home goods online. Formerly known as CSN Stores, it was founded in 2002, and currently offers 14 million items from more than 11,000 global suppliers. The company maintains international operations, including locations in North America and in Canada, Ireland, China and the United Kingdom. Wayfair operates five branded retail websites: the main Wayfair site, Joss & Main, AllModern, Birch Lane, and Perigold.

about: Haleon is a London-based consumer health company, spun out from GSK in 2022, selling over-the-counter and everyday health products such as Sensodyne, Advil, Panadol, Voltaren, Centrum, Nicorette, Otrivin and Parodontax. It sells through pharmacies and supermarkets in more than 100 markets, with revenue about GBP 11bn and around 25,000 staff. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (HLN) and NYSE, with Pfizer having sold its stake. Many household consumer brands, and Haleon uses sports sponsorship such as Sensodyne in football and cricket.

wiki.title: Haleon
wiki.text: Haleon plc is a British multinational consumer healthcare company with headquarters in Weybridge, England. It is one of the largest consumer healthcare businesses in the world, with brands including Sensodyne toothpaste, Panadol and Advil painkillers, and Centrum vitamins. The company was projected to be a global leader in over the counter medicines with a 7.3 per cent market share in 2022. Haleon was established on 18 July 2022 as a corporate spin-off from GSK. Haleon is listed on the London Stock Exchange and is a component of the FTSE 100, with a secondary listing on the New York Stock Exchange.

about: Seagate Technology is a data storage company, legally based in Ireland and operating from Fremont, California, making hard disk drives, SSDs and storage systems for data centers, cloud providers, PCs and consumers. Its Exos drives power cloud storage, and it also sells external drives under Seagate, FireCuda and LaCie, plus Lyve services. Revenue is about $8-9bn. Listed on the Nasdaq (STX). Known by consumers through retail storage products, and a past sponsor of motorsport, including a long relationship with Williams F1 Team.

wiki.title: Seagate Technology
wiki.text: Seagate Technology Holdings plc is an international data storage company. It was incorporated in 1978 as Shugart Technology and commenced business in 1979. Since 2010, the company has been incorporated in Dublin, Ireland, with operational headquarters in Fremont, California, United States. Seagate developed the first 5.25-inch hard disk drive (HDD), the 5-megabyte ST-506, in 1980. They were a major supplier in the microcomputer market during the 1980s, especially after the introduction of the IBM XT in 1983. Much of its growth has come through its acquisition of competitors. In 1989, Seagate acquired Control Data Corporation's Imprimis divisi

about: Amer Sports is a sporting goods group, now headquartered in Helsinki and listed on the NYSE (AS), owning brands including Arc'teryx, Salomon, Wilson, Atomic, Peak Performance and Armada. Revenue is about $6bn. Owned mainly by Chinese investors led by Anta Sports and FountainVest, which bought it in 2019. It sells apparel, footwear and equipment to consumers through retail, wholesale and e-commerce worldwide. Strong consumer brands, particularly Arc'teryx and Salomon, and a regular sports sponsor.

wiki.title: Amer Sports
wiki.text: Amer Sports, Inc. is a Finnish multinational sporting equipment division based in Helsinki, Finland. Established in 1950 as an industrial conglomerate with interests as diverse as tobacco trading, ship owning and publishing, Amer has gradually evolved into a multinational firm devoted to the production and marketing of sporting goods. The company employs over 9,700 people. Since 2018, Amer has been a subsidiary of Chinese retail conglomerate Anta Sports. Amer Sports owns a portfolio of companies, including Atomic, Arc'teryx, Armada, Peak Performance, Salomon, and Wilson, among others.

about: Lazada Group is a Singapore-based e-commerce platform operating marketplaces in Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam. Founded in 2012, it sells products from brands and sellers to consumers and earns commissions, advertising and logistics fees through its Lazada Logistics arm. Majority-owned by Alibaba since 2016-2018. Serves hundreds of millions of consumers across Southeast Asia. Very high consumer brand awareness in the region and previously sponsored sports events such as football.

wiki.title: Lazada
wiki.text: Lazada Group (Chinese: 來贊達; t/a Lazada) is an international e-commerce company and one of the largest e-commerce operators in Southeast Asia, with over 10,000 third-party sellers as of November 2014, and 50 million annual active buyers as of September 2019. Backed by Rocket Internet, Maximilian Bittner founded Lazada in 2012 as a marketplace platform that sells inventory to consumers from its own warehouses. Lazada modified its business model the following year to allow third-party retailers to sell their products on its platform too. The marketplace accounted for 65% of the company's sales in 2014.
